summary: Session 2 of 4 implemented the AccessHarvester classify subcommand: a pure-logic Pipeline layer (RawSchema/ScanConfig/PiiDictionary/ValueFormatDetector/HeuristicsEngine/ClassificationWriter/ClassificationRunner + ISchemaReader/IValueSampler interfaces and a ClassificationDegradation channel), a Core/Com COM-using OleDbDaoSchemaReader (OLE DB TABLES/COLUMNS/PK/FK + DAO AutoNumber + DAO RowSource implicit-FK + linked-table flagging) and OleDbValueSampler (Jet-subquery cardinality, value sampling that never leaks raw values, defensive identifier escaper), and a CLI ClassifyCommand wired into Program.cs with --in / --out / --exclude-cleanup / --json-status. Three rounds of cross-provider verification by gpt-5-4: R1 surfaced 5 issues (lookup-reference category never emitted; incomplete DAO RCW release; identifier escaping + over-broad sampler catches; TryRead*Property too broad; fkTarget.column='*' placeholder + Degradations channel unused) — all 5 fixed. R2 surfaced 4 issues against the R1 fixes (lookup-promotion missed format-pattern columns; rejected identifier aborted scan instead of degrading; TryRead*Property still caught all COMException; composite-FK fallback false-positive) — all 4 fixed. R3 verdict VERIFIED with no further findings. Tests: full suite green (~1900 passing, 2 pre-existing skipped, 1 SkippableFact skipped on Windows-without-COM); 13 new hermetic Pipeline.Tests + 4 new Tests.Classification identifier-escaper tests + 3 new Integration ClassifyCommand tests.

reason.specifics: Session 3 is a single-file zero-install HTML editor (JS + DOM) driven by a finalised JSON schema. The 'open decision' (new repo vs. tools/classification-editor.html) is the only architectural call and is operator-driven. Per project-guidance 'Pin mechanical-correspondence task types to Sonnet rather than Opus', Sonnet at effort=normal fits the cost band; gemini-pro analysis on 2026-05-28 confirmed.
